sources.note: Sec. 4.3 'Jawoyn' (pp. 223-224) treats only lenition of medial singleton stops; 'stress' appears only in the Bininj Gun-wok, Dalabon and Rembarrnga sections (changes in unstressed vowels). No statement of Jawoyn stress placement and no general Gunwinyguan stress statement.

tone.quote: STRESS AND INTONATION Primary stress occurs on the initial syllable of each root except when compounds are formed of more than one root, then primary stress occurs on the penultimate syllable. [ka’ramalk] ’stone axe’ where [malk] is ’digging stick’; [oa’kelkuyi] ’I work’ where the root is [kelku] ’to work’. The basic intonation pattern is a gradual rise culminating in a swift fall at utterance final position for statements, and a gradual rise to utterance final for most questions. [...] NOTES ON OTHER LANGUAGES Gunuwinggu, Djepmi, Djawan, and De?ynekmi have the same phonemic system as Gunbalang.
tone.locator: Appendix I 'Sketch of Gunbalang Phonemics', pp. 172-173, sections 'STRESS AND INTONATION' and 'NOTES ON OTHER LANGUAGES'
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
